**(p. 118) Sūrat al-Aḥqāf (The Sand Dunes)**

Its aim is to warn the disbelievers by showing the truth of the promise of the Hour, which necessarily belongs to might and wisdom, and which reveals both of them in the most complete revelation. This is shown by what has actually occurred of the truth of the promise, namely the destruction of those who denied, through what is contrary to the condition of their lands. Nothing can prevent any of that from taking place, because the one who does it has no partner. So He alone deserves to be worshipped exclusively. The name of the surah, al-Aḥqāf, indicates this, since it signifies the stillness of the wind and the calm of the air. It also points to what the story of the people of Hūd, upon them be peace, reveals: monotheism, their warning of punishment in this world and the next, their destruction, and the fact that what they worshipped did not avail them. It is not correct to name the surah after Hūd, nor to name Hūd after al-Aḥqāf, because of the aim mentioned for each of them.

**"In the name of Allah"**, who is not humbled by whoever sides with Him and is not made mighty by whoever opposes Him; **"the Most Merciful"**, whose mercy precedes His wrath through the admonitions of warning; **"the Especially Merciful"**, who favors His party with the deeds of the righteous, so that they may attain success in the abode of permanence, by entering Paradise and being saved from the Fire.

﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾: the wisdom of Muḥammad (ﷺ), which is the utmost in rightness and soundness. He perfected it, the One whose power encompasses all things, so He does not break the appointed promise.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 2:

When al-Jathiyah was built upon contemplation of the signs of the two horizons (al-khafiqayn), addressed to the people of faith, as an argument for the Day of Decision (yawm al-fasl) indicated in al-Dukhan by the verse: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾ [al-Dukhan: 38] and what follows it, it produced the knowledge that greatness (al-kibriya') belongs to their Creator, as witnessed by His subjugation of kings and others than them to death and what is below it, without concern for anyone. It also made clear, through what kingship, greatness and wisdom convey (for the custom of one who has this attribute is that his speech is only in accordance with need), that the Book is sent down in stages to explain what they attempt, by which it refutes their argument and demolishes their might, by His wisdom and His might. Thus the Gathering (al-hashr) was established and the Resurrection (al-nashr) became due. It concluded with the attributes of might (al-'izzah) and wisdom (al-hikmah). It reminded [them] of all that has been established of that, to confirm the matter of the Resurrection and to verify the Last Day, in a manner that makes clear that all creation is signs, wisdom and lessons, because He established that all of it is true and negated from it every falsehood. So He said, addressing the idolaters of the various religions, the Sabians, the Magians and others, those with whom the surah opened and which was concluded with wickedness (al-fisq), which comprises them and necessitates their disbelief: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, i.e., the one comprising all good through gradual sending down according to what is beneficial, ﴿from Allah﴾ (p-120), i.e., the Almighty, the Proud, the One specified with the attributes of perfection, who is the praise by what His lordship indicates. He concluded with His saying: ﹫the Mighty, the Wise﴾, affirming that He does not place anything except in its most fitting place, and that He is the Creator of evil just as He is the Creator of good and of all actions, and that He honors His friends, humiliates His enemies, and firmly establishes the affair of His religion, making it manifest over all religion, without anyone being able to oppose Him in any part of it. Thus the verse of al-Jathiyah became a premise for this, and this is the conclusion.

(p. 121) When the content of His saying, the Exalted, in al-Dukhan (the Chapter of Smoke) was established in al-Jathiyah (the Kneeling), namely ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play﴾ [al-Dukhan 44:38], through what was mentioned in them of the signs and benefits and wisdoms, He affirmed here the content of what follows that, with the addition of the term, saying, indicating His might and wisdom: ﴿We did not create﴾, that is, by our greatness, which requires exclusivity in majesty, ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, with what is in them of signs, some of which were detailed in al-Jathiyah. Since one of the purposes here is the refutation of the Magians and others who affirmed creation for other than God, He said: ﴿and what is between them﴾, that is, of the air filled with benefits and every good and every evil resulting from the actions of the servants and others. Ibn Burjan said in his tafsir: "The whole of existence, first and last, is a copy (nuskhah) of the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab, the Preserved Tablet), and the heavens and the earth are a reference to part of existence. Part of it gives, in indicating the sought-after matter, what the whole gives in some respect, except that what is higher is more sound in indication, closer in testimony, and clearer in signification, while what is smaller among the existents has a general indication, in which the one who considers it needs care, precision of reflection, and investigation." End of quotation.

﴿except with truth﴾, that is, with the established matter of complete power and absolute disposal. Thus He created falsehood with truth, because it is a disposal in His own dominion, in which no other has any share, for trial and testing, for recompense with justice and bestowal with grace, and for other wisdoms that none but Him knows. In creating these in this manner is the greatest evidence of the existence of the Truth, glory be to Him, and that He is One with no partner, and it indicates His dominance by His saying: ﴿and a specified term﴾, that is, for the resurrection of people to the abode of settlement, for the separation of the people of Paradise from the people of Hellfire, and for the passing away of the two horizons (the heavens and the earth) and what arises from them of night and day.

Since the sense is: "We commanded people to act during that term by obeying Us, and promised them for it the gardens of bliss," then those who believe, in accordance with what they were warned of, are inclined toward it and fearful of its perils, and so they act in obedience to Us; the context ties to it from His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾, that is, concealed from the clear signs what, had they left themselves and had We not created them upon it, they would have known. So they, for that reason, ﴿from what they were warned﴾ (p. 122), from One whom they know does not fail in His warning, ﴿are turning away﴾, and from its perils they feel secure. So they do what angers Us. The signs of existence bore witness before them, yet they did not hear them or give ear to them, and the messengers and books from God warned them, yet they turned away from them and recoiled from them.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, may God have mercy on him, said: When He had mentioned the Book, the greatness of mercy in it, and its sublime clarification, and followed that with what the chapter of the Shari'ah (the Law; i.e., al-Jathiyah) included of rebuke for whoever denied it and severing of their attachments, and that He, glory be to Him, had set up, from the signs of the heavens and the earth [up] to what was mentioned at the beginning of the chapter, each division of which suffices for indication and stands as proof, yet despite this they did not stop persisting in their misguidance and immersion in their evil condition and their wretched state, the chapter of al-Ahqaf was attached, recording their evil deed and informing them of their painful end. So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and a specified term﴾. Had they considered the great interconnection of that truth and its firmness and perfection, they would have known that it was not brought into being in vain. But they were blind to the signs and deviated from following the indications. ﴿And those who disbelieved from what they were warned are turning away﴾. Then He, glory be to Him and exalted, began to reproach and rebuke them for worshipping what neither harms nor benefits, saying: ﴿Have you considered what you invoke besides God﴾ [al-Zumar 39:38], up to His saying: ﴿and they were disbelievers in their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:6]. Then He mentioned their obstinacy in refusing to hear the signs, saying: ﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:7], and so on. Then the speech was joined and interwoven up to the end of the chapter. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 4:

When Allah, glorified is He, had established the principle that proves His oneness, and affirmed justice and the sanctity of the Resurrection for the judgment, and they used to say, "We are the most intelligent of people," and the intelligent person does not feel secure against the dangers of a warning unless he prepares for it something whose repelling is certain, and he cannot repel one who threatens him except someone who equals him or surpasses him, whether by partnership or otherwise, and they used to claim concerning their idols that they were partners, He built upon that principle its branches, and began with refuting their basis of reliance. So He, glorified and exalted is He, said, commanding him ﷺ to alert them to their foolishness, that they had turned away from what could harm them without taking precaution against it, indicating the non-divinity of what they called gods by the absence of any proof of their divinity, whether rational or transmitted, because the station of divinity cannot be established for anything whose exalted rank is known without a conclusive proof: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these who have exposed themselves to the utmost peril, denouncing them in rebuke and reproach: ﴿Have you considered﴾, that is, tell me after reflection and inward sight, ﴿what you call upon﴾, that is, with the call of worship, and He alerted them to their lowliness by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, everything being beneath Him, so that there is no equal to Him.

Since it is known that the question about seeing something whose presence is already known is not valid except by interpreting it as concerning some state, and the sense was: "Show me whether they are partners in the earth?", He resumed with His saying: ﴿Show me﴾, and He emphasized the speech with His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿what they have created﴾, that is, what they have originated, ﴿of the earth﴾, so that the claim that they are partners in it through the origination of that part would be valid. And since the meaning of the speech and its rendering is: "Show me, are they partners in the earth?", He balanced it with His saying: ﴿Or have they a share in the heavens﴾, that is, of those whom you call upon, ﴿a partnership﴾, that is, a kind of partnership: management, as the naturalists say, or creation or other than that. Show me that which they created from them, so that your claim concerning them and your reliance upon them through it may be valid.

So the verse is of the type of ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis): He mentioned creation first as evidence for its omission second, and partnership second as evidence for its omission first.

Since proof is one of two things, hearing (transmission) and reason, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Bring me﴾, [that is], a proof for your claim concerning these idols that they created anything, or that they deserve to be worshipped, ﴿a Book﴾, that is, a single one that may validly be held to, not requiring you to bring more than one book. And since the books are many, and there was no book before the Qur'an that encompasses all of the past times, He introduced the preposition, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿from before this﴾, [that is] the one revealed to me, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, and this is one of the signs of prophethood, for all of them testify to the oneness of God; were any to bring them, they would bear witness against him.

Since He mentioned the highest [proof], which is the conclusive transmitted text, upon which alone obligation is established, He made it easy for them and descended to what is below it, which includes reason, and was content from it with a single remnant, even if it were a trace and not an essence, so He said: ﴿or a remnant﴾, that is, a remainder of a trace suitable for argument. Ibn Burjan said: it is the remainder of the trace of anything that is seen after its passing, and by its trace it is known in its condition of being seen, a successor from a predecessor who relate it in their traces. Al-Baghawi said: the root of the word is from "athar" (trace), which is transmission.

﴿of knowledge﴾, that is, certain, by necessity, experience, observation, or otherwise, even if it were a conjecture indicating what you claim concerning them of partnership. And since they have such aversion to lying, and such abhorrence, repugnance and revulsion toward it as no other nation has, He indicated their rebuke with lying if they do not establish a proof for their claim, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿if you are﴾, that is, with what is innate to you as a disposition, ﴿truthful﴾, that is, firmly established in truthfulness regarding what you claim for yourselves.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 5:

When Allah, glorified and exalted, had refuted their claim about the idols, that they are unable to bring anything of that kind because they are themselves among the created beings in origin, He followed this with a refutation of their claim by their lack of knowledge, so that it would be known with certainty that they are the most misguided of people, since they were bound to the most sublime of matters, which are the foundations of the religion (usul al-din), by something for which there is no evidence at all. So He, exalted is He, said, denouncing that anyone could be more misguided than them, and connecting it to what the context inevitably points to as its implied meaning, which is: "Who is more misguided than one who claims anything at all, however little, without evidence?": ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon﴾ (someone who claims) the greatest of matters without any proof, neither rational (aqli) nor transmitted (naqli). So he ﴿calls upon﴾ what has no power and no knowledge, and whatever lacks both power and knowledge cannot validly be worshipped, by the self-evident judgment of reason (bi-badihat al-'aql). He pointed to their lowliness by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is: from the lowest (p. 127) rank of the ranks of the One who possesses all the attributes of majesty, beauty and perfection. He, glorified is He, knows everything and is capable of everything, so that He answers supplication, removes affliction, fulfills hope when He wills, and manages His servant in accordance with what He knows of his secret and his public affairs, in a way that the servant himself cannot manage his own self by. The servant often desires things which, if he were left to himself and granted his request, would be his destruction; so He, glorified is He, manages him in a way that he hates intensely, and then the situation becomes clear that there was no relief for him except in it. ﴿Who does not respond to him﴾, that is: who does not bring about the response, nor seeks its bringing about from the idols or others, because it has no capacity (ahliyya) for that.

Since the least form of response is simply speech, and they (the idols' worshippers) would be spoken to in the Hereafter in some general sense, even if what was said would harm them, He limited this negation to a time in which no response at all will benefit them, and no one will avail anyone in any way ever. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is: the Day in which We have set forth for them proofs that are clearer than the sun, and which will only increase them in denial and in inclining toward what has no evidence at all, while they claim guidance and most strongly condemn error. Since the one who does not respond may still have (some) knowledge of a person's obedience to him, by which his response might be hoped for at some point, He negated that (p. 128) by His saying, as an added rebuke of them for calling upon what has no hope of benefit: ﴿And they are of their calling unaware﴾, that is: the calling of the polytheists to them. ﴿Unaware﴾, that is: this attribute is fixed in them and they are never free of it; they know neither who calls upon them nor who does not call upon them. He expressed it with heedlessness (al-ghafla), which is among the attributes of rational beings, applied to inanimate things by way of taghlib (applying the term of the more dignified category to the lesser), if what is meant is the general category including the idols and others among the rational worshipped beings of humans, jinn and others; or as a genuine ascription if what is meant is the idols alone; or as a mocking (tahakkum), as if it were said: "They are the knowing ones, for you are too exalted in station to worship what does not reason." Their failure to respond to you at all times is only a constant heedlessness, just as you would say to one who wrote a letter all of which is corrupt: "You are knowledgeable, but you were drowsy," and the like of this.

When He, glory be to Him, set the Day of Resurrection as the limit, it is understood that they will respond to those who called on them on that Day. He then explained what they will say to one another at that time, saying: ﴿And when the people are gathered﴾, i.e., assembled by compulsion, in the easiest manner and with the least effort, ﴿the people﴾, i.e., everyone who is capable of al-nawS (النَّوْس), meaning movement, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿they will be﴾, i.e., those who were called upon, ﴿enemies to them﴾, i.e., to those who called upon them. God will give them the power of speech, so they will address them with everything that an enemy addresses his enemy with. ﴿And they will be﴾, i.e., those who were worshipped, ﴿of their worship﴾, i.e., of those who called upon them, who are the polytheists, ﴿disavowers﴾ of them, ﴿because they were heedless of it, as the Exalted said in Surat Yunus, upon him be prayer and peace (p. 129): ﴿And their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us."﴾ [Yunus: 28]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 7:

When he had made clear that they were in the utmost foolishness in worshipping that for which there is no proof in any way, he followed it with an explanation that they were in the utmost stupidity in denying what nothing is clearer than, so he said, linking it to: ﴿And those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 3]. ﴿And when Our verses are recited﴾, i.e., read by any reciter in the manner of following, ﴿upon them﴾, i.e., the verses that have nothing greater than them in themselves and by their being attributed to Us, ﴿as clear proofs﴾, nothing being clearer than them, they say — this was the original form, but he made clear the attribute that moves them to speak, so he said: ﴿Those who disbelieve say﴾, i.e., they concealed those lights which that recitation had brought forth for them — this was the original form, but he said: ﴿of the truth﴾, i.e., on account of it, ﴿when﴾, i.e., at the time ﴿it came to them﴾, its clarity, since with its clarity there is nothing more firmly established than it, and that they hastened, at the first moment of hearing it, to deny it without reflection: ﴿This﴾, i.e., what was recited, ﴿is sorcery﴾, i.e., imagination with no reality to it, ﴿manifest﴾, i.e., evident that it is imagination. So their saying this — by their hastening to it without any reflection at all, and by its being the furthest of things from the reality of what was said about it — indicates that they are the most obstinate of people and the most audacious in lying, while they claim that they are the most equitable of people and the most committed to truthfulness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 8:

Since these verses have shown, through the greatness of their proofs and the abundance of what their depths contain, that what they profess is weaker than an illusion, and that this Book, in its truthfulness and in every aspect of its affairs, is firmer than the mountains, they were the most worthy of all creatures to say: "We have turned back from what we were in and we have believed." It was the place where it should be said: "Have they acknowledged that you are truthful in attributing this Book to God?" Instead, He balanced it with His words, as evidence for this: ﴿Or do they say﴾, renewing this claim and following it, ﴿he has invented it﴾, meaning: he deliberately fabricated its lie. This would be from their words, a wonder, because it is a statement accompanied by what refutes and nullifies it, as will come in its demonstration.

Since it was as if it had been said: "They do say that, and they have wounded hearts with it, so what turns them back from it?" [It was said]: ﴿Say﴾, which is more painful to them than the impact of arrows, namely that what they have hurled at you is returned upon them by a proof clearer than the sun at midday in a cloudless sky with no cloud between. Since it is the custom of kings that whenever someone lies against them, they hasten to punish him, He said: ﴿If I have invented it﴾, meaning: I deliberately fabricated its lie according to your claim, while I only intend it for your good counsel. Then whatever I invent and attribute to Him, He would punish me for it and would never leave me at all. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿then you would not avail me﴾, meaning: you who are given counsel, at any time and in any way, ﴿against God﴾, meaning: the Supreme King, the Mighty, the Proud, the Wise, ﴿anything﴾ of what would ward off His vengeance upon me; for the king does not leave whoever lies against him in any kind of lie at all. How much more so, then, one who deliberately lies against Him concerning the message, with great matters, and persists in it morning and evening, going and coming. What would then move me to fabricate against Him, when the one aimed at would not benefit me, and the one lied against would not leave me alone? Then He gave a reason, from what the speech conveyed, for the necessity of retribution, with His words: ﴿He knows best﴾, meaning: better than you and better than anyone, ﴿about what you are busy with﴾ of attributing lies to me. Had it been as you say, He would not have debated with me, let alone confirmed and supported me. In this there is a threat to them, consolation for him, and relief from him.

Since dictation alone is not decisive in this matter, though it is apparent in it, a decisive proof and a shining demonstration were necessary for the claim of truthfulness. The testimony of the King, about whom the speech is, was the greatest of proofs, because He is the most knowing, and the basis of testimony is knowledge. So the speech definitively produced His words: ﴿is sufficient﴾, and it emphasized the speech by what was joined to the subject of the preposition, to confirm the act and negate metaphor, so He said: ﴿as a witness between me and you﴾, meaning: a witness of eloquent testimony, because He is the most knowing of all our states. ﴿He bears witness by His own Most Holy Self to the truthful one among us, and against the liar.﴾ He has testified to my truthfulness by your inability to produce anything like this Book that I brought. Thereby it became established that it is His speech, because I am not able, by myself, to do what you are not able to do, whether individually or collectively, while you are Arabs like me. Indeed I am ummi (unlettered), and among you are the scribes and those who mixed with the scholars, heard the narrations of the nations, and traveled the lands of the Arabs after the lands of the 'ajam (non-Arabs). Thus it became manifest, as clear as the sun, that you are liars. ﴿And He is the Forgiving﴾, the One whose nature is to erase sins entirely, both their essence and their traces, so that He does not punish for them or reproach. ﴿the Merciful﴾, who bestows honor after forgiveness and favors with success in what pleases Him. In this conclusion there is encouragement for the Prophet (ﷺ) to pardon them for what they attributed to him at the beginning of it, of fabrication; an exhortation to good conduct toward them; an encouragement for them to repent; and a prohibition against their saying: "Why does He not hasten the punishment upon us for our attribution of lying to you, if you are truthful?" by the principle that He may grant respite to the liar. As for His supporting him with what strengthens his truth, which would necessarily mean He increases the lie in him, that is not permissible, because that would be a flaw in wisdom, in majesty, and in sovereignty.

(p-133) Since it is among the greatest of errors that a person be attributed with lying in a matter that he did not originate, when a people before him had done the same, whose truthfulness in such matters had been established, and the ages had passed over it, and it had become firmly settled in hearts and minds to the utmost degree of firmness, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these who attributed fabrication to you: ﴿"I am not a novelty"﴾, that is, I am not one who innovates, originates, creates, or invents, such that I would be a stranger, cut off ﴿from the messengers﴾, having no precedent among them for the basic thing I have brought, which is the matter over which the dispute between me and you has been prolonged and the affair has grown great, namely Tawhid (the affirmation of Allah's oneness) and the noble qualities of character. Rather, many messengers preceded me who came with the like of what I came with and called to it as I called, and Allah confirmed them with the like of what He confirmed me with. Thereby their messages were established, and whoever among their peoples affirmed them was made happy by them, and whoever denied them was made wretched by them. So look at their traces, and ask about their biographies from their followers, helpers, and partisans.

The Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz said in his Diwan: "Bid'ah (innovation) is the name for what has been innovated, and its opposite is the Sunnah, because the Sunnah is that for which an imam has preceded, while bid'ah is what is invented without a precedent." And in the hadith: "Every bid'ah is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire." Its meaning, and Allah knows best, is that one innovates what opposes the Sunnah, since bid'ah is the opposite of Sunnah. So when one introduces what opposes it (p-134), by his introducing it he is astray and a polytheist, and whoever introduces such is in the Fire. This does not include what a person devises of acts of righteousness, which is called bid'ah because it was not done before. That falls outside what we have mentioned if it has a counterpart in the principles, namely the urging toward all acts of righteousness, whether known or unknown. If an innovator introduces something of that kind, it is as though it were an addition to the righteousness that preceded it, and it is not a contrary to the Sunnah that came before it; rather it is a door of its doors.

They say: "So-and-so is no novelty in this matter," meaning he is not the first to whom that befell, but others preceded him in it as well. The poet said:

"I am no novelty among the calamities, the breaking of misfortunes and their passing over."

It is also said: "Ubdi'a bi-l-rajul" when his mount becomes exhausted, and "abda'at al-rikab" when the mounts become exhausted and perish. It was said: whoever's mount perishes and he is left stranded has been "ubdi'a bihi." In the Qamus: "Bid'ah: a new thing in religion after completion, or what is newly introduced after him ﷺ of desires and deeds," and "Ubdi'a bi-l-rajul: his mount perished," and he remained cut off, and "Ab'da'a fulan bi-fulan": he abandoned him and forsook him, (p-135) and did not attend to his need; and "his proof was voided." Al-Saghani said in Majma' al-Bahrayn: "Shay'un bid' (with kasra), i.e., muktada' (innovated); and fulan bid' fi hadha al-amr, i.e., badi' (wondrous/unprecedented); and qawm abda'; from al-Akhfash: al-badi' is the innovated and also the innovator. And 'ubdi'at hujjat fulan': if it was voided. And 'ubdi'at': it was nullified; it is transitive and intransitive."

When He established, through his ﷺ agreement with the messengers, the basic principle of the speech, and what remained was to be said—that the denial concerned whether Allah had sent him with it—the proof of his truthfulness in his claim was established, namely that he is similar to them in the basic creation; he has of his own essence no knowledge beyond what they have, and none of them is valid in ruling on unseen matters. So were it not that Allah had sent him, it would not be valid that everything he judged regarding future matters would come true without any exception. Thus He said: ﴿"And I do not know"﴾, that is, in this state, by any kind of stratagem, action, or effort, ﴿"what"﴾ [i.e., which] ﴿"will be done"﴾, that is, by whatever doer [it may be], whether it is Allah the Exalted directly or through an intermediary [other than Him], ﴿"with me"﴾. He emphasized the negation so that it would be evident in the collective and likewise in the individual: ﴿"nor"﴾ [i.e., nor do I know what will be done] ﴿"with you"﴾. This is in the basic creation. And you see me judging about myself with things that never fail, such as my saying: "I bring you from the Qur'an (p-136) what will defeat you, and none of you will be able to oppose any part of it," and this holds true continually without ever failing at all. Were it not that Allah sent me with it, I would not, alone, be able to do what none of you can do. And if I were able to do something, you would be more able than I to do it. The verse, in its generality, is evidence that Allah may do what He wills: He may punish the obedient and bless the disobedient, and if He did so, it would be justice and truth, although we believe that He does not do it.

When He made His noble self equal to them in the basic creation, and Allah had distinguished him from them by what He specified for him of prophethood and messengerhood, He, glorified and exalted, brought that out as a conclusion, saying: ﴿"I follow"﴾, that is, with the utmost of my effort and diligence, ﴿"only what"﴾, that is, what ﴿"is revealed"﴾, that is, whose delivery is renewed, from the One who reveals nothing truthfully but Him, ﴿"to me"﴾ by way of gradual descent, secretly, which no one other than me fully comprehends, and among it is that about which I am informed of unseen matters, so it comes to pass as I said. Thus no one doubts that I am not able to do that by myself, and it is known that it is from Allah.

When they attributed to him fabrication at one time and madness at another, and the greatest cause of their attributing that to him was his proclaiming what displeased them, contrary to his former habit and the habit of his like, He said, by way of qasr qalbi (restriction by reversal): ﴿"And I am not"﴾, that is, (p-137) by my informing you of what is revealed to me, ﴿"except a warner"﴾, that is, to you and to everyone the Qur'an has reached, ﴿"clear"﴾, that is, manifest, that I am so in myself, making it manifest to all—that is, my being a warner—and to all the particulars from which I warn, by definitive proofs.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 10:**

When he had established that it is from Allah, by the testimony of Allah Himself, through their inability to produce its equal (mu'arada), it was reprehensible of them to persist in denial, on the assumption that someone whom they trust among the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) testifies to it, and they ask him about it. So the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Have you considered?﴾, that is: inform me, make clear to me, and establish, even with some part of an argument or a proof, ﴿if it was from Allah﴾, that is: this which is revealed to me and which I bring to you, with which I warn you and inform you that it is from Allah, then indeed it is ﴿from Allah﴾, that is: the Supreme King.

Since the purpose of the surah is to warn the disbelievers who do not reflect upon knowledge, and whose way is to conceal the known truths and sciences, He joined the clauses with the conjunction "wa" (and), which indicates mere togetherness that comprises the joining of the two matters without any delay, and thus it indicates haste in disbelief without reflection. [He] said: ﴿and you disbelieve in it﴾, that is: on this assumption. ﴿And a witness testified﴾, that is: one or more ﴿from the Children of Israel﴾, whom your custom was to consult and trust, ﴿to its like﴾, that is: the like of what is in the Qur'an (p-138) that whoever affirms Divine unity has believed, whoever associates partners has disbelieved, and that Allah sent this down in the Torah, the Gospel, and all their books. Their books agreed upon it, their messengers supported it, and their prophets, peace be upon them, repeatedly called to it and commanded it. Then he made his testimony the cause, followed it, and detailed it, saying: ﴿and believed﴾, that is: this one who gave this testimony, upon seeing this Qur'an confirming what was mentioned and knowing that it is the Book which their scriptures gave good news of, so he was guided to placing a thing in its proper place, and he placed it there and did not become arrogant.

Since the factor that drove them, after these proofs, to persist in disbelief was nothing but obstinacy and haughtiness, He said: ﴿and you were arrogant﴾, that is: you created arrogance by turning away from it, seeking by that leadership, pride, and prestige. Thus, after the testimony of this witness, you were stubborn without any doubt at all, and you went astray [and disbelieved], placing a thing in other than its place, so the door of guidance was closed to you.

Since they claimed that they were the most rightly guided of people and the most just, and since whoever rejects the testimony of the Creator and the creation is a severe wrongdoer, he was misguided with knowledge. Allah the Exalted said, beginning a new clause and indicating that the implied answer is: Have you not, by your abstention from faith after knowledge, wronged yourselves with a great wrong by placing disbelief in the place of faith, so that you have become misguided, abandoning the path that leads to it deliberately? ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, that is: the Supreme King (p-139), possessor of might and wisdom, ﴿does not guide the people﴾, that is: those who have the capacity to accomplish what they seek to attempt, ﴿the wrongdoers﴾, that is: those whose nature is to place matters in other than their proper places. Therefore He does not guide you, because there is no one more deeply rooted in the wrong that has caused your misguidance than you. As for whoever among you is learned, the matter is clear concerning him; and as for whoever among you is ignorant, he is like the learned one, for his failure to reflect on such proofs, which lie between the one who knows the language of the Arabs and the revelation of these matters to him, is only the reflection upon them together with the abandonment of desire. Al-Hasan said, as transmitted by al-Baghawi, that the answer is: ﴿Who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?﴾, as He said in Fussilat:

﴿Say: Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in far-reaching opposition?﴾ [Fussilat: 52]

So the verse is of the device of al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two contrasting elements are mentioned, each one implying the other): He mentioned faith first as evidence of its opposite second, and arrogance, wrongdoing, and non-guidance second as evidence of their opposites first. Its secret is that He mentioned the two causes of happiness, as encouragement and as warning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 11:

When he had shown that their abandonment of faith was in fact a deliberate act of wrongdoing born of arrogance, he followed their saying "it is plain magic" with what points to arrogance, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed﴾, that is, they deliberately covered up the truth, ﴿"If it had been good﴾, that is, for the sake of the faith of those who believed, since they preceded them to faith, ﴿"— if their belief in the Qur'an and in this Messenger were good﴾, that is, among the sum of goods, ﴿"they would not have preceded us to it.﴾ And we are more noble than them, and greater in wealth and children, and more knowledgeable in attaining honour and lordship, which is the basis of good. So it is as though they had not preceded us to anything of these goods in which we are triumphant and they are empty-handed. But it is not good, and therefore they preceded us to it." [So] their state regarding it was like their state regarding what is perceptible of their affairs, in wealth and standing.

When he had reported what they said when others preceded them, he reported what they say when they deliberately turn away from it, saying: ﴿And when they are not guided by it﴾, that is, and when they do not take guidance from it, saying, out of obstinacy, arrogance and disbelief: "If it had been guidance, we would have seen it." They did not know that it is not the eyes that go blind, but the hearts that are within the breasts that go blind.

Since the implied sense is: "If it is said to them, 'Then what is it?'", he answered that by His saying, giving a cause for this implied matter, as one of the signs of prophethood: ﴿So they will say﴾, with a promise that admits no failure, because people are enemies of what they do not know, and because they found no proof for their claim that, had it been good, they would have preceded others to it: ﴿"This is an ancient lie"﴾, that is, something turned away from its face to its back, ﴿"ancient."﴾ Someone else lied and they came upon it, brought it, and attributed it to God.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 12:

Since this statement (of the disbelievers) is by itself baseless, because of the compelling proofs that have been established for the truthfulness of the Qur'an (p-141), and since staring at perceptible things was generally dominant among them, owing to their lack of penetration into intelligibles, (God) indicated its falsehood by the agreement of the Qur'an with the greatest of earlier books, the Torah, which is well known to be from God, and that the one who brought it was spoken to by God. God confirmed him in bringing it with the miracles and clear signs that he had not brought before. And they were asking the People of the Book (for guidance). So He said, in a manner of rebuke and reproach: ﴿And before it﴾, i.e., they said this while it was in some of the time that was before it, i.e., the Great Qur'an, whose verses they were deprived of contemplating and whose difficulties they were deprived of resolving, and whose eloquence overwhelmed them: ﴿was the Book of Moses﴾, the one who was spoken to by God and His chosen one, upon him be peace, and it is the Torah with which God spoke to him with direct speech, while its Book was ﴿a guide﴾, i.e., deserving that everyone who heard of it should take it as a guide in the fundamentals of religion absolutely and in all that it contains before its distortion, abrogation and alteration. ﴿And a mercy﴾, because of the blessing it contains of indicating God and its sufficient explanation. So even if they criticized this Qur'an, they are not able to criticize the Book of Moses, which they have granted to its people as being people of knowledge and made them judges, whose word they accept about this noble Prophet. Their own book confirms it (p-142), so by this they have become confirmers of what they denied. For this reason God the Exalted said: ﴿And this﴾, i.e., the clear, explaining Qur'an, ﴿is a Book﴾, i.e., one comprising all good things. When the confirmation of all divine books and legal rights was intended to be generalized, He omitted the object and said: ﴿confirming﴾, i.e., confirming the Book of Moses, upon him be peace, and other books whose ascription to God the Exalted is valid; for all the books brought by the messengers testify to the Oneness of God, and this Book has not departed from this. So how could it be valid, regarding something of this nature, that it be a lie? The lie is only what denies the books of God which His prophets brought and which His friends inherited.

Since the Book is one whose agreement with the books of God is established by proofs, and it is in a language other than that of the one who denies it, the denial would be less blameworthy. He guarded against this by His saying: ﴿in Arabic tongue﴾, i.e., this confirmer is pointed out as being close to you in time, place and understanding, while being ﴿Arabic﴾ at the highest levels of the Arabic tongue, together with being the easiest of books to take up and the furthest from burdensome. It is not such that its loftiness through the grandeur of its words, the majesty of its meanings, the elevation of its arrangement, the excellence of its composition, the brevity of its expression (p-143), the manifestness of its meanings and the subtlety of its allusion would prevent it from being easily understood, with nearness of approach after the remoteness of the aim.

When He indicated that the Book is true, He explained its fruit, so He said: ﴿to warn﴾, i.e., the Book is indicated in this state, [in order that the Book warn] by the excellence of its exposition and the greatness of its status, ﴿those who have done wrong﴾, whether they are deeply rooted in wrongdoing or not. As for those deeply rooted, for them there is a complete warning, for they will not be guided, as was mentioned before. As for others, they are guided by its warning and become happy through its expression and allusion. And ﴿to give good tidings to the doers of good﴾ at some time — "at some time" being "good tidings" complete — ﴿to the good-doers﴾, for whom there is no warning, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. So the verse is of the type called ihtibak (interlocking omission): it mentioned first "warn" and "those who have done wrong," indicating the omission of [its counterpart second, and "good tidings" and "to the good-doers" second, indicating] "my warnings" and "for the wrongdoers" first.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 13:

When he had explained the condition of the people of ihsan (doing good), he elaborated on their affair, saying, resuming in answer to one who asked about them and about their glad tidings: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾, i.e., our Creator, our Master, and the One who does good to us, ﴿Allah﴾, glorified and exalted is He, and none other. And since istiqamah (steadfastness, meaning firmness in everything that pleases [Allah], together with its being consequent upon tawhid) is a noble attainment of lofty rank, and since it is generally not reached except after lengthy struggles and severe striving, he indicated both its remoteness and the height of its rank by the particle of delayed sequence, saying: ﴿Then﴾, i.e., [after] their saying that by which they affirmed the oneness [of Allah], ﴿they were steadfast﴾ (p-144), i.e., [they sought] the goal with a great seeking and actualized it.

Since the description applies to the leaders of the believers, he counted their deeds as causes, and so he informed about them with his saying: ﴿there will be no fear upon them﴾, i.e., it will not overwhelm them with the predominance of harm. Perhaps he expresses this in such a context with the nominal form, indicating that awe of Him, in view of His majesty, dominance, might, greatness and perfection, does not cease, and that by calling it to mind a person attains humility, tranquility, dignity and serenity, which increase him in his own soul in majesty, elevation and perfection. Thus what is negated is a fear that disturbs the soul, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, in their inner selves or outward appearance, ﴿they will grieve﴾, i.e., there will recur to them any sorrow at all.

When He had negated for them what is feared, He supplied them with what they prefer, that which brings joy. So the Exalted said: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the possessors of the high ranks, ﴿are the companions of the Garden﴾. Since "companionship" indicates constant attachment, He stated it explicitly with His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾, an abiding that has no end. They are recompensed with this ﴿as a reward﴾. Since they were doers of good, and their deeds were in the utmost sincerity, He made them causes, first and second, and He said, pointing to their continuity because they are in their innate natures: ﴿for what they used to do﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿they were doing﴾, in the manner of constant, continuous renewal.

[p. 145] When Allah, glorified and exalted, had bestowed His favour upon man after the deeds for which He prepared him, empowered him to perform them, and granted him success in them through means, He joined the command to obey Him, since He is the Originator (al-Mubdi'), with the charge concerning parents, since He made them the means of bringing him into existence. So He said, in this context, in which He enumerated the deeds (the context of ihsan, i.e., excellence and beneficence), the best of which is prayer at its appointed times, and second in rank is kindness to one's parents, as in the Sahih and in al-Tirmidhi: "The pleasure of Allah lies in the pleasure of the parents, and His displeasure lies in their displeasure." In this same manner the custom of the Qur'an has run: it enjoins obedience to parents after the command to worship Him, as in ﴿And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel: Worship none but Allah, and be good to parents﴾ [al-Baqarah: 83], and ﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents﴾ [al-Nisa': 36]. Likewise what follows these, by way of coordination with what I have estimated, or with the surah, [such as] saying: "And We commanded all people that they should, within the appointed term of life, act in obedience to Us and avoid disobeying Us." ﴿And We enjoined upon man﴾, i.e., this kind which is intimate with itself, ﴿regarding his parents﴾. Since "wassa" (enjoined) has fulfilled its two objects, the implied sense is: that he should treat them well. The Kufans read ﴿ihsanan﴾ (goodness), and it is more fitting to the context.

Since the right of the father is manifest, in that he has no part in earning, spending, protecting, and disciplining (the child) in this sense, he did not mention it; and he mentioned what is due to the mother, because her period (of service) is brief, so she may be belittled. Hence he said, beginning a new statement or giving a reason: ﴿His mother bore him﴾, i.e., after his father had placed him, by sharing with her in her womb, a bearing ﴿in hardship﴾, with the heaviness of pregnancy, its illnesses, afflictions, and symptoms, ﴿and bore him in hardship﴾, i.e., after the completion of the period of his gestation [al-Fussilat: 11]. This indicates, along with its indication of the obligation of the mother's right, that the matter of his formation belongs to Allah alone. He mentioned the middle of what is due to the mother, in terms of the period of hardship, by mentioning the minimum period of gestation and the maximum period of breastfeeding, because they are fixed, so he said, may He be exalted: ﴿His gestation and weaning is thirty months﴾, i.e., the period of his gestation and the ultimate limit of his weaning from nursing. He expressed it by "fisal" (weaning) to signify the end point, because weaning may occur before the end point for some purpose, and then the need appears and nursing is resumed. Thus "fisal" refers to the complete period mentioned in al-Baqarah. From this it is known that the minimum period of gestation is six months, and the physicians hold this view. It may also suggest that the minimum period of nursing is one year and nine months, because the most common period of gestation is nine months.

Since what follows this sometimes involves both parents sharing in his maintenance and sometimes one of them alone, he omitted mention of them both and used the particle of limit (hatta) to divide the one enjoined into two categories: the obedient and the disobedient, mentioning for each what is due in reward, as good tidings and warning, guiding to the meaning: and he continued, each of them, upon his parents or one of them. ﴿Until, when he reaches his full strength﴾. Al-Fayruzabadi said in al-Qamus: "Its strength, and it is between eighteen years and thirty years. Ashudd is one word that came in the form of a plural, like anuk, and there is no parallel to these two; or it is a plural with no singular from its own form; or its singular is shiddah (with a kasrah), though fi'lah is not pluralized on the pattern af'ul; or it is shadd, like kalb and aklub, or shidd, like dhi'b and adhu'ub; and these two are not heard (in usage) but are analogical." End of quotation.

What has passed in Surah Yusuf is very useful here. Al-Tabarani narrated in the biography of Ibn Ahmad ibn Labid al-Bayrutiyy, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "The ashudd is thirty-three years, and it is the age at which 'Isa ibn Maryam was raised up." Al-Haythami said: "In its chain is Sadaqah ibn Yazid, whom Abu Zur'ah and Abu Hatim declared trustworthy, and Ahmad and a group weakened; and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." Al-Zamakhshari said: "It is the beginning of the ashudd, and its limit is forty."

Although the days of youth and early manhood are the choicest period of a person's life, and the times of his delight, the gathering of his affairs, and his comforts, in them the secret of his life usually becomes apparent to him, owing to the predominance over him of base, bestial, and predatory souls, through what those two bring upon him of the consequences of appetites, the impulses of anger, and idleness, [p. 148] he expressed it with what indicates barrenness, ill omen, and constriction, as an alert to this. So he said, explaining and expressing the state of equilibrium: ﴿And reaches forty years﴾. Thus his full strength gathered, his resolve and diligence were perfected, and the wildness of youth, the giddiness of early life, and the recklessness of ignorance departed from him. For this reason this age was the time of the sending of the prophets, and it suggests that the periods of youth are lighter in accountability than what follows them, and likewise what lies between the beginning of ashudd and forty. ﴿He says﴾, if he is one who does good and is receptive to the charge of his Lord: ﴿My Lord﴾, i.e., O You who do good to me by bringing me into existence, facilitating my parents and others, and subjecting them for me, ﴿enable me﴾, i.e., make me able ﴿to be grateful for Your favour﴾, i.e., making me one who is restraining (wazi') for gratitude, i.e., restrained and bound, so that it does not overcome me at any time. That gratitude is by monotheism in worship, just as He is singled out in the favour of bringing into existence and provision; and He mentioned it in the singular to magnify the matter, by indicating that a single favour cannot be fully thanked except with Allah's help. Yet the mention of the two parents shows that what is meant by it is the genus.

Since perhaps someone may suppose that what is meant by His favour is His power to bestow, so that the meaning would be: "that I may thank You for being able to bestow," he said: ﴿which You have bestowed upon me﴾, [p. 149] i.e., in actuality, since that is obligatory upon me by His particular favour to me, ﴿and upon my parents﴾, even if only by the general bringing into existence and bodily well-being, because the favour upon them is a favour upon me. What has passed in al-Naml contains what must be kept in mind here.

Since the greatest aim of the past favour, namely the favour of bringing into existence, whose gratitude is monotheism, he followed it with the completion of gratitude, saying: ﴿And that I do righteousness﴾, i.e., I myself, in my own person, ﴿righteous﴾. Since the righteous deed in itself may fall short of its proper place because it lacks permission, he said: ﴿that You are pleased with﴾. The indefiniteness (in "righteous") indicates inability to attain the goal, for no one will measure Allah with His true measure.

Since he invoked for himself after he had enjoined attention to the right of his father, Allah, glorified, taught him the supplication for those who descend from him, urging the observance of their rights, lest they be empowered over him in disobedience. So he said: ﴿And make righteous﴾, i.e., bring about righteousness, ﴿for me in my offspring﴾, because their righteousness reaches him as benefit. The purpose of restricting the verb and making them a place (of it) is that it should be firm, established, and pervasive among them while they encompass it, so that they become righteous.

Since he recalled, at the perfection of intellect at forty, that most of the life that had passed had been wasted, he supplicated; and since repentance is a condition for the acceptance of supplication, he gave the reason with his saying: ﴿Indeed I have repented﴾, i.e., I have returned ﴿to You﴾, i.e., from everything that impairs turning toward You, [p. 150] and he emphasized it to inform that his state of inclining toward appetites was the state of one for whom abandoning them is remote, so that the report of it might be denied; and likewise his saying: ﴿And indeed I am of the Muslims﴾, i.e., those who submit outwardly and inwardly to You, and yield to You in the most complete and finest submission.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 16:

When he had described this believer, beginning with him because he is in the context of goodness (al-ihsan), and since the intended meaning of "al-insan" (the human being) is the category as a whole, He said, praising him in the plural form, drawing attention to the fact that the acceptance of acts of obedience is conditional upon kindness to one's parents, because what appears is evidence of what is hidden. Whoever does not thank the one who is of his kind, especially one who is closest to him, and especially one who is the cause of his existence, has not thanked God, as in the hadith: "He who does not thank people does not thank God." Whoever sets right what is between himself and [God, sets right what is between himself and] people in general, especially his relatives by lineage or by place, and especially his parents: ﴿Those﴾, that is, those of high rank, ﴿from whom We accept﴾ in the easiest manner ﴿their best deeds﴾. By the verbal form "natakabbalu" (taqabbal, the form of ta'aqqul, "to accept"), He indicated that in accepting it He acted like one who takes care. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read with the nun (we) in it and in the following verb. What confirms this is His saying: ﴿the best﴾. It is also possible that what is meant is the absolute of supplication or acts of obedience, and that what falls short of the best is accepted, an absolute acceptance according to the measure of intention in it. The use of "ʿan" (from) for the transitive construction indicates that their natures are built upon ascending the ladders of perfection at every time, without end. Thus these good deeds are not [from them] in the sense that they are naturally inclined toward something higher than them at their final stages, and the consideration is for final stages. For this reason He said: ﴿what they did﴾ and did not say "their deeds."

Since the human being is a locus of deficiency even if he is a doer of good, He drew attention to this, and to the fact that the condition for the expiation of misdeeds is repentance, by His saying: ﴿and We overlook﴾, that is, with a promise that is accepted, which must be present. This is the meaning of the recitation of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i with the nun in both verbs ﴿their misdeeds﴾, that is, He does not punish them for them.

Since this implies that they are among the people of Paradise, He stated it explicitly, increasing their praise, by His saying: ﴿among the companions of the Garden﴾, that is, He did that for them while they are among them, because they never ceased to be in it, since they never departed from the state of contentment. Since this is a promise, He confirmed its content by His saying: ﴿the true promise﴾, because it corresponds (p-152) to reality, ﴿which they were﴾ with a firmly established state ﴿being promised﴾, that is, the promise of it was made to them in the world by one who is more truthful than them, namely the Messengers, upon them be blessings and peace.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 17:

When Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned this doer of good first, because the context is one of goodness, He followed him with the doer of evil, which suits the purpose of the surah stated explicitly at its opening. He said, exalted is He: ﴿And one who says to his parents﴾, while they are both together, ungrateful for their blessings and rejecting Our injunction concerning them. So he was ungrateful for the blessing of the greatest perceptible benefactor after disbelieving in the blessings of the greatest benefactor absolutely. The dual form indicates that he is the harshest of people in heart, because it is customary for a person to accept the words of his origin even if it is one (parent), and that togetherness in general has an influence, so how much more when it is a parent. ﴿Uff﴾, that is: impatience, disgust, contempt, and aversion from me. Its dialects are forty, as reported in the Qamus (a lexicon). The variants transmitted from the reciters (qira'at, recitational readings) are three. The kasr without tanwin (nunation), which is the reading of the majority, means that the meaning intended is linked to a fixed lowliness. With tanwin, which is the reading of the Medinans (al-Madaniyyin) and Hafs, it means a great lowliness that continues over time with dominance and subjugation. The fath without tanwin, which is the reading of Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub, means the intended meaning is joined with fame for loftiness and spread, together with permanence. It has already been mentioned in (the commentary on) al-Isra' from al-Harrali, and this is the correct view, that ta'fif (saying "uff") is the most complete and severe form of harm, for its meaning is that the one said "uff" to has no worth or weight at all, and is fit for nothing; rather he is nonexistent, and non-existence is better than him, along with the utmost filth.

Since it was as if it were said, "For whom is this uff?", He said: ﴿For you both﴾. And since they were as if they had said to him, "Why this great disdain after the kindness, you cannot repay us for it?", He said, rebuking, reproaching, and denouncing them, rejecting the assumption that it is a promise: ﴿Do you promise me﴾, that is, continuously and repeatedly at all times, ﴿that I will be brought forth﴾ [that is] from an exit by which something brings me out of the earth after I have been hidden in it and have become dust, to be revived as I was the first time. ﴿And [already] have passed away﴾, that is, while the state is that they have already gone before and passed on, following the ways of death, ﴿generations﴾, that is, the many ages of their hardness. The preposition (min) is used because a generation (qarn) does not come to an end except after a long period, so the passing away in that is not all-encompassing of time. He said: ﴿before me﴾, that is, generation after generation and nation after nation, and times have been prolonged, and most of them deny this account, so I am with the majority. This is supported by the fact that none of them has returned. ﴿And they both﴾, that is, while the state is that whenever he said that to them, ﴿seek help from Allah﴾, that is, they ask, through their supplication, the One who possesses all perfection to help them by inspiring him to accept their words, saying to their son, striving in counsel for him after striving in supplication: ﴿Woe to you﴾, as a compassionate person says when distress increases in him and grief reaches him, indicating that if he turns away there remains for him nothing but woe, which is destruction. ﴿Believe﴾, that is, bring about the faith that is no faith other than it, which is what rescues from every destruction and causes every success, by affirming the resurrection and everything that has come from Allah. Then they gave their reason for their command in this manner, emphasizing in response to his denial, and said: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾, that is, of the greatest King, encompassing all attributes of majesty and perfection, described with might and wisdom, ﴿is true﴾, that is, established with the greatest establishment, because if it were not true it would be a deficiency in terms of breaking promises, which the least of the Arabs would not accept for himself; how much more so, since it would entail the contradiction of wisdom, by making creation in that case a matter of futility, because they are servants and subjects who will not be presented before their King who originated them, despite His knowledge of their injustice to one another and the transgression of some against others. ﴿Then he says﴾, as a consequence of their statement and following it: ﴿This is not﴾, that is, what you have told me about resurrection, ﴿except legends of the former people﴾, that is, fables that the ancients wrote in falsehood, and which generations transmitted from them, generation after generation, until they became such that the weak believe they are authentic. This is all the more astonishing, since by believing it one is not necessarily subjected to corruption under any of the possible assumptions; rather, belief leads him to good deeds and noble morals, which he himself acknowledges to be good, such as adhering to the path of goodness and abandoning the path of evil. Whereas denying it drags him to exultation, insolence, arrogance, evil deeds, and base morals, along with the possibility of the destruction with which they threatened him. And although he considers it unlikely, it does not negate that it is possible. What they called him to, as you see, is not repugnant to any rational person, but these are minds that their Creator has deceived.

(p-156) Now, since this discourse, together with its reaching the utmost in excellence of arrangement, has laid out these two categories as an eloquent parable for the disbelievers of the Arabs and their believers, the first being for the believers who follow the creed (millah) of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, which was brought by the greatest of his noble prophets, Muhammad, may the best of prayers and peace be upon him, and the second being for the disbelievers who reject the greatest of their forefathers, Ibrahim, peace be upon him, whom they know through a transmitted report which they inherited from their fathers, and through an inimitable Qur'an, as though they had heard it from their Creator, that he (Ibrahim) was a monotheist, affirmed the Resurrection, and warned against its perils. He, glorified is He, had begun speaking about them with what He mentioned of their disbelief concerning the favoured ones, and they deserved both disgraces, the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. He informed about them of what their denial of their Lord's promise and their disobedience to their parents produced, in reality or as instruction, by His saying: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the distant ones [from] intellect, manliness, and every good, ﴿upon whom the word has come into effect﴾, that is, it has been established and become due. Since this was a threat, He indicated it with the particle of elevation, so He said: ﴿upon them is the word﴾, that is, the perfect word in its kind, that they are the lowest of the low. This refutes those who said that it was revealed about ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn [Abi] Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both; for he embraced Islam and became one of the great Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all, so Paradise was made due to him.

(p-157) When He established for them this abomination, He identified the multitude of those who shared in it, so He said: ﴿among﴾, that is, existing within ﴿nations﴾, that is, multitudes who were such that people would pursue them and some would follow others, ﴿that have passed away﴾, those nations. Since the one judged was some of the earlier ones, He introduced the preposition, so He said: ﴿before them﴾, so they were their exemplars, ﴿of the jinn﴾. He began with them because the Arabs held them in awe and sought their protection; that is because they would appear to them and harm them, and nothing cut off their harm and their domination over them, outwardly and inwardly, except the Qur'an; for it burned them with its lights and expelled them from those lands by its manifest traces. ﴿And of mankind﴾, and their great numbers did not benefit them nor did their strength avail them. Then he gave a reason for the obligation of the command upon them, or began a new statement with the following words, emphasizing them as a refutation of the assumption of this category, about which the discourse is, that the correct view lies with the majority: ﴿Indeed they﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿were﴾, that is, by nature, disposition and character, unable to disengage from it, ﴿losers﴾, that is, deeply immersed in this attribute.

ولَمّا قَسَّمَهم في الأعْمالِ، جَمَعَهم في العَدْلِ والإفْضالِ فَقالَ: ﴿ولِكُلٍّ﴾ أيْ: مِن فَرِيقَيِ السُّعَداءِ والبُعَداءِ مِنَ القَبِيلَتَيْنِ: الجِنِّ (p-١٥٨) والإنْسِ، في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ ﴿دَرَجاتٌ﴾ أيْ: دِرْكاتٌ؛ أيْ مَنازِلُ ومَراتِبُ مُتَفاضِلِينَ فِيها "مَن" أجْلِ "ما عَمِلُوا" أوْ مِن جَوْهَرِهِ ونَوْعِهِ مِنَ الأعْمالِ الصّالِحَةِ والطّالِحَةِ. ولَمّا كانَ التَّقْدِيرُ: لِيَظْهَرَ ظُهُورًا بَيِّنًا أنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ فاعِلٌ بِالِاخْتِيارِ بِالمُفاوَتَةِ بَيْنَ العُقَلاءِ ويَظْهَرُ بَيِّنًا لا وقْفَةَ فِيهِ أنَّ الحَقائِقَ عَلى غَيْرِ ما كانَ يَتَراءى لَهم في الدُّنْيا؛ فَإنَّ حُجُبَ المَكارِهِ والشَّهَواتِ كانَتْ تُرِي الأُمُورَ عَلى خِلافِ ما هي عَلَيْهِ، عَطَفَ عَلَيْهِ قَوْلَهُ في قِراءَةِ البَصْرِيِّينَ وعاصِمٍ وهِشامٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عامِرٍ بِخِلافٍ عَنْهُ: ﴿ولِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ﴾ أيْ: رَبُّهُمُ الَّذِي تَقَدَّمَ إقْبالُ المُحْسِنِ عَلَيْهِ ودُعاؤُهُ لَهُ، وقِراءَةُ الباقِينَ بِالنُّونِ أنْسَبُ لِمَطْلَعِ السُّورَةِ ولِما يُشِيرُ إلَيْهِ مِن كَشْفِ حُجُبِ الكِبْرِياءِ في يَوْمِ الفَصْلِ.

ولَمّا كانَ سُبْحانَهُ يَعْلَمُ مَثاقِيلَ الذَّرِّ وما دُونَها وما فَوْقَها ويَجْعَلُ الجَزاءَ عَلى حَسَبِها في المِقْدارِ والشَّبَهِ والجِنْسِ والنَّوْعِ والشَّخْصِ حَتّى يَكادَ يَظُنُّ العامِلُ أنَّ الجَزاءَ هو العَمَلُ قالَ: ﴿أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ أيْ: جَزاءَها مِن خَيْرٍ وشَرٍّ وجَنَّةٍ ونارٍ - وهَذا ظاهِرٌ، أوْ نَصٌّ في أنَّ الجِنَّ يُثابُونَ بِالإحْسانِ كَما يُعاقَبُونَ بِالعِصْيانِ، وسُورَةُ الرَّحْمَنِ كُلُّها خِطابٌ لِلثَّقَلَيْنِ (p-١٥٩) بِالثَّوابِ لِأهْلِ الطّاعَةِ، والعِقابِ لِأهْلِ المَعْصِيَةِ مِن كُلٍّ مِنَ القَبِيلَتَيْنِ؛ كَما سَيَأْتِي إنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ تَعالى بَيانُهُ، ويُجْزى مُطِيعُهم بِالثَّوابِ كَما يُجازى عاصِيهِمْ بِالعِقابِ - قالَهُ مالِكٌ وابْنُ أبِي لَيْلى والضَّحّاكُ وغَيْرُهم كَما نَقَلَهُ البَغَوِيُّ.

﴿وهُمْ﴾ أيْ: والحالُ أنَّهم ﴿لا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ أيْ: لا يَتَجَدَّدُ لَهم شَيْءٌ مِن ظالِمٍ ما مِن ظُلْمٍ في جَزاءِ أعْمالِهِمْ بِزِيادَةٍ في عِقابٍ أوْ نَقْصٍ مِن ثَوابٍ، بَلِ الرَّحْمانِيَّةُ كَما كانَتْ لَهم في الدُّنْيا فَهي لَهم في الآخِرَةِ فَلا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أحَدًا بِأنْ يُعَذِّبَهُ فَوْقَ ما يَسْتَحِقُّهُ مِنَ العِقابِ، أوْ يَنْقُصَهُ عَمّا يَسْتَأْهِلُ مِنَ الثَّوابِ.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 20:

Since the dominant theme of this surah is warning (indhar), as its opening attests, he says, mentioning some of what the guilty will be rebuked with on the Day of Resurrection, the day they used to deny, and in which the recompense for deeds is fully paid, linking it to a implied sense: "Recount this to them, perhaps they will be too proud to be evildoers and so become among the good-doers": ﴿And the day﴾, that is, and recount to them the day ﴿when they are exposed﴾. This was the original form, but He made apparent the attribute that necessitates their recompense, indicating that the matter was evident to them, yet they veiled the lights of their intellects. So He said: ﴿Those who disbelieved are exposed﴾, that is, of the two groups mentioned, ﴿to the Fire﴾, that is, they are scorched by its flame and turned over in it, as meat is exposed to be roasted, being told by way of reproach, rebuke, censure and denunciation (p-160) because they did not remember God as He should be remembered in their desires, but rather obtained them while opposing His command and prohibition, the Glorified: ﴿You squandered﴾. It is read with the declarative form by Nafi', Abu 'Amr and the Kufans, while the rest read it as an interrogative, for added denial and rebuke. ﴿Your good things﴾, that is, your pleasures by following your desires ﴿in your life﴾, and He made it abhorrent by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the worldly﴾, that is, the near and lowly, whose description informs those who understand of another life after it. So your striving in your movements and your stillnesses was for its sake, until you attained it. ﴿And you enjoyed﴾, that is, you sought and brought about your benefit ﴿from them﴾, and made them the utmost of your portion in your elevation and your bounty.

Since this was contempt for the commands and prohibitions, owing to contempt for the Day of Recompense, He made His saying, exalted is He, a consequence of it: ﴿So today you will be recompensed﴾, that is, for your turning away from Us, with the recompense of one whom you cannot escape from its requital by the easiest matter from Him: ﴿the punishment of humiliation﴾, that is, the great, gathered, severe disgrace in which there is abasement and ignominy, ﴿for what you used to be﴾ by nature and disposition ﴿arrogant﴾, that is, seeking elevation and bringing it about continuously ﴿in the earth﴾, which, because it is dust and set for passing away and ruin, (p-161) is the most deserving of humility, lowliness and abasement. Since arrogance may be in truth, as it is against the wrongdoers and thus praiseworthy, He restricted it by His saying: ﴿without right﴾, that is, a matter to which reality conforms, namely Our commands and Our prohibitions. By the particle of completeness He indicated that He does not punish for arrogance under doubt. ﴿And for what you used to be﴾ continuously ﴿defiantly disobedient﴾, that is, renewing your departure from the sphere of obedience to which the primordial nature and the intellect call, toward the impulses of sins.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 21:

When Allah, glorified is He, had warned them of the matters of the Hereafter, and He concealed the command to remind them of these, because they are hidden, while they deny them, in His saying "wa-yawma" (and the Day), and He concluded with punishment for the blameworthy arrogance and the transgression, He followed it with a warning to them concerning matters that are perceptible, because they are bound by them, explicitly stating the command to remember. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Remember﴾, meaning: to these people who do not take heed, with the place of wisdom which is not hidden from anyone of intellect, and it is the Resurrection. Since the most suitable thing with which they are threatened in this surah, and the most appropriate to its purpose, is their being the strongest of people in bodies, the most stubborn in their necks, the hardest of hearts, the most extensive in dominion, and the greatest in arrogance, to the extent that they used to say ﴿Who is stronger than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat: 15], and they built the building which outlasts time and does not perish, and none would build such except one who forgot death or hoped for eternity, and they made a garden on the face of the earth, because their kingdom encompassed all of it, along with the nearness of their lands, since they were in the lands of the Arabs, from Quraysh, and their knowledge of their news and their seeing of their dwellings, and because their punishment arose from their land by the supplication of one of them, He mentioned their matter in a manner which indicates the purpose of the surah. He expressed it with brotherhood to console His Prophet ﷺ, because the atrocity of a people against one who is from among them, and who knows his virtues and glories, is more painful. So He said: ﴿the brother of 'Ad﴾, and he is the brother of Hud, peace be upon him, who was among a people whom your people do not match in strength or power, and who nevertheless declared to them the bitter truth and confronted them with the command of Allah, did not fear their consequence, and We saved him from them. So he is an example for you and there is a model in him, and for your people, in their intent to harm you, there is an admonition from his affair.

When He, peace be upon him, reminded him of these exalted purposes, He substituted for it his story as an added clarification, and He said, making clear that warning is the greatest purpose of the message: ﴿when﴾, meaning: at the time when ﴿he warned his people﴾, meaning: those who had surplus strength beyond what they attempted to do, ﴿in al-Ahqaf﴾. Al-Asbahani said: Ibn 'Abbas said: it is a valley between 'Uman and Mahrah. He said: Muqatil said: the dwellings of 'Ad were in Yemen, in Hadramawt, at a place called Mahrah, to which the Mahri camels are attributed, and they were people of mobile pillars in spring, and when the grass dried they returned to their dwellings. They were from the tribe of Iram. Qatadah said: they were overlooking the sea in a land called al-Shajar. Al-Ahqaf is the plural of hiqf (a sand-dune), with a kasra, and it is sand that is elongated, raised, with a curve in it. Ibn Zayd said: it is what extends from the sand like the shape of a mountain without reaching the level of a mountain. In the Qamus (al-Qamus al-Muhit, the lexicon) it says: it is the great, rounded sand, and the origin of the sand; and "ihqawqafa" (the sand, the back, and the crescent) meant: it lengthened and curved. From what is clear is that this formation does not occur in lands where the wind is dominant and severe, because if that were so it would have blown the mountain away with a blowing, unlike the mountainous lands such as the noble Makkah, where the wind is extremely severe there, for it either strikes the mountain and rebounds with a severe force, or there are mountains between which it is pushed back, or it is compressed and comes out through the gaps it finds in a disturbing manner. Therefore, the people of the mountains should be more cautious than that.

When He mentioned the warner and the warned, and their place with respect to what was mentioned of the purposes, He mentioned that (p. 164) they turned away from him, and this was not a novelty among the messengers, nor were his people ignorant of their conditions, so they deserved punishment as a warning against the likes of their state. So He said: ﴿And indeed﴾, meaning: and the situation is that indeed ﴿there had passed﴾, meaning: had gone by, elapsed, and died ﴿the warners﴾, meaning: the many messengers whose station of command was warning.

Since their sending had not actually encompassed all times, He introduced the preposition, and said: ﴿from before him﴾, meaning: before him, like Noah, Seth, and Adam, peace be upon them, so he was not a novelty among them; ﴿and from behind him﴾, meaning: those who came after him, so you are not a novelty among them. When He indicated the multitude of messengers, He mentioned their unity in the fundamental call, so He said, explaining the warning and expressing it in the form of a prohibition: ﴿that you worship not﴾, meaning: O servants who are warned, in any way whatsoever, anything of things ﴿except Allah﴾, the King, for whom there is no king other than Him, and no creator besides Him, and no bestower of blessings except Him. Indeed I see you associating with Him what did not associate with Him in any part of your management, and a king does not approve of the like of this.

When He had commanded and forbidden them, He gave the reason for that, saying, warning them of the punishment, emphasizing their denial because of their reliance on the strength of their bodies and the greatness of their status: ﴿Indeed I fear for you﴾, because you are my people and the most beloved of people to me, ﴿the punishment of a great Day﴾ which leaves no direction without filling it with its punishment, if you persist in what you are in of association.

(p-165) When the listener was eager to hear their answer concerning this wisdom, the reply came in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said﴾, i.e., denying against him: ﴿"Have you come to us﴾, i.e., O Hud, ﴿to turn us away﴾, i.e., to divert us from the direction of our affair to its back, ﴿from our gods﴾, so that we do not worship them nor give them any regard." And since the meaning of denial is negation, the sense was: "We will not turn away from them." They then made a consequence of this their saying, ﴿"So bring us what you threaten us with"﴾; they called the threat a promise, mocking him. And since that meant denying him, they added clarity to it by saying, using the particle of doubt, as an indication that his truthfulness in this is a matter of supposing the impossible: ﴿"If you are"﴾, i.e., as it is said of you, a constant state ﴿"one of the truthful"﴾ in that you are a messenger from God and that He will bring us what you fear for us of punishment if we persist.

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 46, verse 23:

Since their statement contained an attribution to their caller, upon him be blessings and peace, of something that his words do not indicate in any way, namely a claim to knowledge of their punishment and power over it, and a denial of both, which necessarily entails [their security, which entails] their claim to know that they will not be punished, and they were lying in all of that, it is as if it were said: (p-166) "With what did he answer them?" So it was said: ﴿He said﴾, confirming them in denying him knowledge of that and power over it, and refuting them in their attribution to him of a claim to either of these two, and in their attribution to themselves of the claim that it will not happen: ﴿The knowledge is only with Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything, your punishment and other things, ﴿with Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection. So He sends down the knowledge of what you are promised upon whom He wills, if He wills, and I do not have knowledge of it now, nor do you have any of that or any power over it.
