Since comprehensive knowledge entails power, the meaning is: the power to bring about your punishment belongs only to Him, glorified and exalted be He, not to me or to anyone else, and upon me there is only conveyance, as my Lord revealed to me in His words, glorified be He: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance﴾ [al-Shura: 48]. And I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you, the admonition that your deeds are the deeds of one who has turned away from his master and exposed himself to ruin and punishment by associating with the Absolutely Benevolent one who is in no way comparable to Him, so he is in a state where he is feared to be seized. He then joined to this his words: ﴿And I convey to you﴾, that is, also now and in the future, ﴿what I have been sent﴾, that is, by the One who in reality has no sender other than Him, for He is able to support His messenger ﴿with it﴾ (p-167), that is, with the Oneness of God and other things, whether it is a promise, a warning, or something else, even if the end were not mentioned, because what he was sent with is suitable for them and for others.

Since the meaning of the report of conveyance is that upon me there is only that, and since the meaning of restricting absolute knowledge to Allah is confirming them in their denial of his knowledge of that, upon him be blessings and peace, it was fitting for him to say, as a correction of his knowledge against their ignorance: ﴿But I see you﴾, that is, I know you with a knowledge that is like seeing, ﴿a people﴾ who are harsh, severe, and insolent, ﴿who are ignorant﴾, that is, [with you] together with that, the attribute of ignorance, which is harshness in other than its proper place along with little knowledge. You renew, for yourselves, [continuously, because] you act by associating with the Absolutely Benevolent one, and [He is] the Supreme King, one who has no benevolence in any way, the deeds of one who deserves punishment. Then you do not consider its occurrence possible, and you deny the one who warns you that this is a matter that must be guarded against, and you attribute to him what he was not sent for, namely warning, by claiming power over punishment and the like.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 24:

Since their saying this brought about the coming of the punishment, [so that it came upon them] as a black cloud, they persisted in their ignorance and in their habit of feeling secure and not deeming retribution possible (p-168). It was as if its coming were close to their seeking it hastily, and therefore he used the fa' (so, then) in His saying, causing it to follow from their denial, clarifying the magnitude of their ignorance through their ignorance regarding perceptible things, detailing what their state was when they saw the calamity: ﴿So when they saw it﴾, meaning the punishment with which he had threatened them, ﴿as a cloud approaching them﴾, meaning a black cloud appearing on the horizon, plainly evident to one who has the capacity for observation, while it was heading [toward them] ﴿facing their valleys﴾, meaning seeking to be opposite them and bringing that about. It is a description of "cloud" (ʿāriḍan), so it is indefinite though its genitive construction is verbal (lafẓiyyah), even though it is attached to a definite noun; likewise "mumṭiranā" (bringing us rain). ﴿They said﴾, in keeping with their habit of ignorance, pointing to it with the particle of proximity which indicates that they were at the utmost of ignorance, because their ignorance of it persisted until it nearly overtook them: ﴿This is a cloud﴾, meaning a cloud spread across the breadth of the sky, that is its side, ﴿bringing us rain﴾, because they saw it black and heavy, so they thought it was full of water by which they would be relieved after a long drought, and after they had sent their envoys to blessed Mecca to pray for them there to God, whom they had treated lightly by impugning His sovereignty, by associating with Him those who are beneath them, knowing that their partners would avail them nothing in bringing rain, heedless of their sins which necessitated their punishment. Therefore God, the Exalted, said, turning away from their words, and it is apparent that it is a quotation (p-169) of the speech of Hūd, peace be upon him, in reply to their words: ﴿Nay, it is what you sought to hasten﴾, meaning this cloud which you see is what you sought to hasten in its coming to you, of the punishment.

When the listener's eagerness to know it became intense, He said: ﴿A wind﴾, meaning it piled up this cloud which you saw, ﴿in which is a painful punishment﴾, meaning severely painful. It used to carry the howdah in the air, carrying it and its occupant until it appeared like a locust, and they would see what was outside their dwellings of people and livestock being carried aloft by the wind between heaven and earth, then it would hurl them down.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 25:**

﴿Tudammiru﴾ means: it destroys, with a great, severe, and swift destruction; it comes suddenly, in the manner of an assault, ﴿everything﴾, meaning: [it overtakes it]. Such is its nature. Whoever is spared from it, like Hud, upon him be peace, and those who believed in him, may God be pleased with them, their survival is an extraordinary matter that breaks the normal custom, just as its command to destroy everything it passes over is an extraordinary matter that breaks the normal custom. The two clauses may be understood as a description of the wind. It is also possible, and this is sweeter, more stirring to the soul, and more wondrous, that they are a resumptive clause (isti'naf, a new independent sentence). Since someone might think that the wind acts by its own power, He said (p-170): ﴿by the command of its Lord﴾, meaning: the One who originates it, nurtures it, and bestows favour upon His servants by using it to take vengeance on His enemies.

When He mentioned it with this awesome mention, and the implied sense was: they were visited by it, and it destroyed them, leaving none of them, He made the following a consequence of that, as an intensification of the awe: ﴿So they became﴾. When the hearer's attention intensified regarding the manner of their morning, He said, translating their destruction: ﴿you could not see﴾, meaning: you, O beholder. When the heart's terror and the soul's dread became great, Exalted is He, said: ﴿except their dwellings﴾, meaning: as a recompense for their crimes. Thus the expression matched the meaning. It is known that by "morning" is meant mere existence, but it was expressed with it because the calamity in it is greater. It is also known that no dwelling of the deniers remained, nor any blower of a fire. This is a kinaya (metonymy) for the generality of their destruction, whether the sand buried them or they were laid out on the face of the earth in rows, as in the other verse:

﴿So you see the people in it lying prostrate as if they were trunks of hollow palm trees﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7]. It is narrated that when Hud, upon him be peace, sensed the wind, he withdrew with those who believed with him into an enclosure. The wind then swept over the disbelievers, onto al-Ahqaf, which was their gathering place when they spoke and the place where they spread out when they played. They remained beneath it for seven nights and eight days. Then it lifted from them, carried them away, and hurled them into the sea. Likewise it destroyed their livestock and everything among their possessions that had a soul. It did not harm Hud, upon him be peace, and those with him, may God be pleased with them, [from it], except that it softened their skins and revived their spirits. According to this, the verse is to be taken in its literal sense: the morning did not dawn while any of them was seen.

When hearts flew away with this terror and minds were bewildered, Exalted is He said, drawing attention to the essence of the meaning by way of istinaf: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning: like this recompense, awesome in its origin, its kind, its type, or its individual form, of destruction ﴿We recompense﴾ with Our majesty, always, whenever We wish, ﴿the people﴾, even if they are at the height of their strength, ﴿who are criminals﴾, meaning: those who are deeply steeped in crime, who sever what ought to be joined and join what ought to be severed. That recompense is destruction in this shameful manner. So beware, O Arabs, of the like of this, if you do not return.

When this was a context in which information about the state of their power was expected, so that it would be known whether they had abandoned repelling [the punishment] because of some obstacle within them, or because what came to them was such that no one could repel it, He said, mentioning the particle of expectation (*qad*) to frighten the Arabs, swearing an oath, because one of Quraysh had said that they would repel the punishment by repelling the Zabaniyah (the angels of hell) and the like: ﴿And We had certainly established them﴾, meaning, this was done to them while the state was that We, by Our might, had established them in a way through which Our greatness appears [p. 172] ﴿in that wherein We did not establish you﴾, meaning, in that which We did not establish you in, of bodily strength, abundance of wealth, and other things. He made the negation "in" (*in*) rather than "ma" (*ma*), because *in* is more emphatic than *ma*, since *ma* negates the complete attainment, being composed of the *mim* and the *alif*, whose reality of perception is the loss of complete perception, whereas *in* negates the least manifestation of what follows it, so how much more so the completeness of it. This is because the *hamza* is the first manifestation of the loss of the *alif* and the *nun* for mere manifestation. Beyond this, there is the sweetness of the utterance and its preservation from the heaviness of repetition, and other wondrous secrets.

Since Quraysh took pride in their intellects, they perhaps thought that in reason and its prerequisites, the senses, they were more capable than them, and that what came upon them was only due to their lack of understanding, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We made﴾, meaning, a making befitting what "We added to you" of capacity, in accordance with what Our greatness required, ﴿for them hearing﴾. He began with it because the context is one of warning that alerts through the sense of hearing to what is in the visible signs of admonitions, and it is more beneficial because it is clearer. He made it singular because there is little variation in it. ﴿And sights﴾, meaning, alerting to what is in the visible signs of the correspondence of their reality to the reports of hearing, [p. 173] and He made it plural because there is great variation in the lights of the sights. Likewise in His saying: ﴿and hearts﴾, meaning, hearts, so that by them they might know the truth and follow it, and the falsehood and avoid it, and be grateful to the One who bestowed them upon them. He concluded with them because they are the ultimate goal, beyond which there is no endpoint of perception and no target beyond it. He expressed it with what derives from *tafawwud* (the sense of emptying out), which is detachment, indicating that they are at the peak of intelligence. ﴿But their hearing did not avail them﴾, at the time of Our sending to them the mercy through the tongue of Our Prophet Hud, peace be upon him, and then the vengeance by the hand of the wind, ﴿nor their sights﴾. He emphasized the negation by repeating the negating particle, so He said: ﴿nor their sights﴾. Likewise in His saying: ﴿nor their hearts﴾, meaning, when We wanted to destroy them. He emphasized it by affirming the preposition, so He said: ﴿of anything﴾, [meaning] of benefit, however little, [not] in repelling the punishment, nor in knowing what is right. Rather, they diverted what We had bestowed upon them of faculties to what is not fitting to fix aspirations upon, of worldly affairs, until they surpassed the nations in that and acted as those who think themselves eternal, as it is said:

*And ʿĀd did strive for eternity, but they did not become eternal.*

When He mentioned the negation of benefit, He mentioned its time in a way that conveys causation, for when vengeance is mentioned at the time of an act, it is known that its cause is that act. So He said: [p. 174] ﴿because they used﴾, meaning, as a natural disposition and character for them, ﴿to deny﴾, meaning, to repeatedly reject over the passage of time, ﴿the signs of God﴾, meaning, denial of what is known from the proofs of the Supreme King. ﴿And there encompassed﴾, meaning, there surrounded, in the manner of burning and greatness, ﴿them﴾ with matters from which they did not know the way of escape, ﴿that which﴾, meaning, the punishment of that which ﴿they used﴾, in the manner of continuity, because it had become a character for them, ﴿to mock﴾, meaning, they bring it about continually, as one who seeks it and is passionate about it brings it about.

When the purpose of the report about their destruction was complete, given the great power they possessed, so that whoever heard their story might take warning from them, He followed up with those who had shared with them in denial and therefore shared with them in destruction. He said, repeating it to frighten them and indicating that His power encompasses by the comprehensiveness of His knowledge:

﴿And We had certainly destroyed﴾ by the great majesty and the all-encompassing power that We possess, which have preceded all that We will, ﴿what is around you﴾, that is, O people of Makkah, ﴿of the towns﴾, like the people of al-Hijr, Saba', Madyan, the People of the Thicket (al-Aykah), the people of Lut, Pharaoh, the companions of the Rass, Thamud, and others among those in whom there is a lesson. Since the thing they were admonished with was destruction, it was mentioned first, so the listener became eager to ask about their condition in the verses. Thus He said, (p-175) conjoining with the particle "wa" (and), whose conjunct does not require that it precede what it is conjoined to: ﴿And We have varied the signs﴾, that is, We turned the clear proofs about and repeated them, making them connected, detailed, adorned, and beautiful, in many aspects of indication, free of every doubt.

Since the variation of the signs does not single out any particular person, but is for everyone who sees them or hears of them, He did not restrict them to those people, and He mentioned the all-inclusive reason that applies to others as well. He said: ﴿so that they might return﴾, that is, the disbelievers, ﴿might return﴾, meaning that in the sight of one who knows their condition, in the seeing of the signs, they would be like one who turns back from the error he was riding, whether through imitation or doubt, which the signs uncovered and the proofs exposed. But they did not return, so their not returning was the cause of Our destroying them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 28:

When they had made the focus of their position the associates, claiming that they were the cause of mutual connection among them and of differing in rank, and asserting that they would intercede for them, bringing them near to God in nearness (zulfa) and protecting them from punishment in the Hereafter, and when the lowest of matters was equating Him with the punishment of this world, He (exalted) connected to His report about the destruction of the earlier nations His saying, presenting the cause which they had made the focus of their consideration, disapproving of them and rebuking them: ﴿Why then did they not help them﴾, that is: is it not so, and why not, ﴿those whom they took﴾, that is, these destroyed ones, ﴿besides God﴾, that is, besides the King who is greater than every great one, ﴿as offerings﴾, that is, for the sake of nearness and great drawing-near, they drew near to them and claimed that they would bring them close to God, ﴿as gods﴾, whom they associated with the Greatest King for this very reason. May God fight them and disgrace them.

Since specification (al-takhsis) implies that they did not help them, He turned away from that and said: ﴿Nay, they strayed﴾, that is, they vanished and became blind to the straightest path and went far away ﴿from them﴾ at the time when the vengeance descended and the punishment befell, physically and spiritually. Since the implied sense was: that taking, to which their extremely base intellects led them, far from rightness, was what brought them to this end, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And that﴾, that is, the far-off straying from correctness which was gathered from this story, the reversal of what they used to say: that their idols were gods, that they harm and benefit, that they bring them near to God and intercede for them with Him, ﴿was their lie﴾, that is, their turning of affairs from their proper face to their backs. It may also be that the reference is to the punishment, meaning: this punishment ﴿was their recompense﴾ in return for their lie, ﴿and they used to﴾, that is, on a continuous basis, since it was in their natures, ﴿fabricate﴾, that is, deliberately lie about it; for their persistence in it after the coming of the signs can only be due to that, since whoever considers them stripped of desire would be guided.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 29:

When what has been mentioned of their distance from faith, together with the varied admonitions, lessons, and signs, was almost going to make the listener despair of the faith of these people being addressed, He brought him near by way of indicating His might and wisdom, by reminding him of faith from among those who were higher than them in rebelliousness, more intense in aversion, further from responding, and more hidden in person. So He said, as an answer to what befell him ﷺ when he presented his noble self [to] the tribes and they turned away from him, especially the people of al-Ta'if, indicating the perfection of power, as good news to the one sent down upon [him] ﷺ and as a rebuke for those among his people who were slow to respond to him, connecting it to what is presumed to be: Mention these reports. ﴿And when﴾, that is, and mention the time when ﴿We turned toward you﴾, that is, We directed you with a pure, good, and firm direction, inclining toward you, facing you, and turning away from others, at Wadi Nakhla, on your return from al-Ta'if, when you presented your noble self to them after the death of the two helpers, and they rejected you with a rejection that nearly splits the gall bladders and makes the eyes shrink away from its remembrance.

When seeking the inclination of one who is created with aversion, and displaying [the favor] to one who is built upon concealment, is greater in blessing, He expressed it with what indicates that, and said: ﴿a company﴾. It is a term applied to fewer than ten, and this is what is meant here; it is also applied to all people. The goodness of expressing it with this is that these, since they were singled out for the honor of precedence and the goodness of following, were as if they were the company and no others. ﴿of the jinn﴾, from the people of Nusaybin, from the region from which 'Addas came, whom We made to console you in al-Ta'if, by his testimony to his two masters, 'Utba and Shayba, the sons of Rabi'a, that you are the best of the people of the earth. Yet these company have from their natures nothing but aversion and concealment, and concealment is hiding and covering. So We made them companions for you, appearing before you, so that they might convey to them what We sent you with; for We sent you to all creation. This is a consolation for you and good news of the belief of those who flee from mankind, just as We supported you with them after the aversion of the people of al-Ta'if through 'Addas. Then He described them by His saying: ﴿who listen to the Qur'an﴾, that is, they seek to hear the remembrance that gathers every good and distinguishes between every confusion. And you were at the dawn prayer at Nakhla, leading your companions in prayer. [p. 178]

And He indicated the nearness of the time of the turning from the time of the presence by His, may He be exalted, expressing it with the particle "fa" (then) in His saying, may He be exalted, detailing their condition: ﴿So when they attended it﴾, that is, they came to a state in which they heard it. ﴿they said﴾, that is, some of them said and the others approved: ﴿Be silent﴾, that is, be quiet, incline with your whole selves, and listen, observing courtesy upon the carpet of service. In this is courtesy with knowledge in its acquisition, and also with its teacher. Al-Qushayri said: The people of presence are characterized by humility, stillness, awe, and gravity, while agitation and disturbance indicate absence or a lack of alertness and a deficiency in insight. It also indicates that what they heard was little and its time was short, and [it indicates] the detailing of their condition after its conclusion by the "fa" in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when﴾, that is, so when they were silent, ﴿it was concluded﴾, that is, the recitation was finished, which indicates its greatness, whoever the reciter was, ﴿they turned back﴾, that is, they performed the turning, which is nearness, by directing faces, aspirations, and resolves [p. 179] ﴿to their people﴾ who have the strength to carry out what they attempt. And this indicates the goodness of their acceptance of what they heard and their firmness in its belief by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿as warners﴾, that is, warning them and cautioning them against the consequences of error, by an order from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made them messengers to their people. [p. 180]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 30:

As if it had been asked, "What did they say to their people when warning them?", it was answered: ﴿They said﴾, that is, to their people, when they turned toward them: ﴿O our people﴾, showing tenderness toward them and compassion for them by mentioning what indicates that they were from among them: what concerns them concerns the speakers, and what distresses them distresses the speakers, as it has been said:

*"Indeed your true brother is the one who stays with you, and the one who harms himself for your benefit."*

Since they knew, from the descent of what is in the books of the prophets of the Children of Israel, the Psalms, and the Gospel, that these books were devoid of rulings and legal limits except for a little of that in the Gospel, they were certain, or as good as certain, that no book would descend that compares with the Torah in rulings, legal limits (p-181) and other matters. So when their people might hesitate to report the descent of something more noble than that, they emphasised their statement: ﴿Indeed we have heard﴾, that is, between us and the reciter there is an intermediary. They also indicated that after the Torah nothing had descended that comprehends all that is intended from it and suffices without all other books except this one. Through this they knew that it is abrogating (naskh) for all the sacred laws. So, as a clarification of what they heard, they said: ﴿a Book﴾, that is, a comprehensive reminder, unlike what descended after the Torah upon the Children of Israel, ﴿sent down﴾, that is, from One other than whom there is no true sender, the Owner of the Kingdom and the King of kings. For upon it is the splendour of the divine books that necessitates certainty for its hearer that it is one of them. How much more so when miraculousness is added to that. They knew with certainty from its Arabic eloquence that it was in Arabic, and that they used to travel to the east and west of the earth and hear people's recitations of the wisdoms, sermons, soothsaying, letters and poems they produced, and that this (Book) is distinct from all of that, being recently sent down from the place of greatness. So they said, affirming the preposition: ﴿after Moses﴾, peace be upon him. They did not count what was sent down between this Book and the Torah, such as the Gospel and what preceded it, because it does not equal the Torah in comprehensiveness, nor does it match this Book in rulings, judgment, subtleties and admonitions, (p-182) together with the miraculousness and other qualities it adds.

When they reported that it was sent down, they followed it with what attests to its truth. So they said: ﴿confirming what is before it﴾, that is, of all the books of the Children of Israel, the Gospel and what preceded it. Then they explained its confirmation by their saying: ﴿guides to the truth﴾, that is, to the established matter to which reality conforms, so that no one can remove anything of what it reports, complete in all of that; ﴿and to a straight path﴾ that leads to the greatest goal, which is belief in the One who sent it down. ﴿It is straight﴾, so it leads with the greatest possible speed, and no crookedness can be in it. Thus the traveller on it is able to shorten a route that would be a straight line, as opposed to what curves from it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 31:

When they had informed their people about the Book, and had made clear that it is from Allah, and that it is the nearest means of reaching Him, their people were bound to ask: "What, then, should we do?" They answered them with His words: ﴿O our people!﴾, meaning those who possess strength of knowledge and action, ﴿respond to the caller of Allah﴾, that is, to the Greatest King, who encompasses the attributes of majesty, beauty and perfection. The call of this Caller is general to all creation, so responding is obligatory upon everyone whose affair has reached him.

Since the one who responds may respond in some matters and not others, as Abu Talib, the paternal uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ), did, they joined in their address to them regarding the call, saying: ﴿and believe in him﴾, that is, let your assent be caused by the Caller and by no other cause. For the object of "with" (al-maf'ul ma'ahu) is an object together with the one who sent him, who is Allah, whose power is exalted. Believe in Him from every denial. Or the pronoun refers to the one who is added to, [and he is Allah], as shown by their saying: ﴿He will forgive you﴾, for He covers and overlooks, ﴿from your sins﴾, that is, shirk and what resembles it of what is a right of Allah, the Exalted. That covering will not occur unless you respond fully and assent fully. They included [“min” (from)] to inform that the wrongs done to people are not forgiven except by appeasing their owners. Likewise, what a person is requited for in this world through punishments, calamities, griefs and the like, which is indicated by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30].

﴿and He will protect you﴾, that is, He will shield you, ﹝if you respond﹞, as a neighbor shields his neighbor, because by aligning yourselves with His caller you have become of his party, ﴿from a painful punishment﴾. Their limiting themselves to forgiveness is a reminder of their sins, because their purpose was warning. This does not contradict the explicit statement in this [surah]: ﴿For each there are degrees according to what they did﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 19], which affirms reward. Abu Hayyan transmitted from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "They will have reward and they will have punishment; they will meet in Paradise and throng at its gates."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 32:

When they had finished with making the Truth known, pointing to it, calling to it, and warning gently, with what their speech conveyed, namely that if they did not respond, He would take vengeance upon them with painful punishment, they followed this with what is more severe in warning than that, saying: ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah﴾, i.e., does not renew his response to ﴿the caller of Allah﴾, that is, the Greatest King, Encompassing of all things, to whom none is equal and against whose wrath no one has any power, so that the call of this Messenger ﷺ encompassed all creation.

When the Book and the Sunnah, as I mentioned in the surahs al-An'am and al-Furqan, indicated the universality of the Message, and the one who abstains from responding to one whose message is universal is a disobedient person deserving of punishment, He expressed his punishment with what indicates its certainty, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿then he cannot escape [Allah] in the earth﴾, i.e., from what He decrees against him, ﴿in the earth﴾, for it is a sign that He has made a path through it, so he is within His dominion, His possession and His power, which encompasses him. ﴿And he will have no protectors besides Him﴾, i.e., besides Allah, who grants protection to none but Him, ﴿protectors﴾ who would do for his sake what a relative does for his relative of defending him, interceding for him, ransoming him, and taking his side for his sake.

When escape from Him was negated from every direction, and this does not differ whether the disobedient one is one person or more, the speech of Him, glorified and exalted is He, produced the plural form (p-185) because it is more indicative of power and shows that the disobedient are many, since sins suit most natures: ﴿Those are in clear error﴾, i.e., those far removed from every good, ﴿in clear error﴾, i.e., evident in itself that it is error, making manifest to everyone the ugliness of their being encompassed by it. Al-Qushayri said: It is said: Response is of two kinds: the response of Allah and the response of the caller. The response of the caller is by witnessing the intermediary, who is the Messenger ﷺ; and the response of Allah is openly when the Messenger's message ﷺ reaches the one called, through the envoy, and secretly when the knowledges arrive upon the heart from the inspirations. So one responds with his self, responds with his heart, responds with his spirit, and responds with his inner secret; and whoever holds back from the call of the caller to him is abandoned, and is no longer addressed by it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 46, verse 33:

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had completed what the central aim (*maqṣūd*) of this surah required, namely the fundamentals of the religion (*uṣūl al-dīn*, the core beliefs) and its branches (*furū'*, the derived rulings), and the warning against His seizures (*saṭawāt*) through mention of some of His exemplary punishments (*mathulāt*), and concluded with the misguidance of those who did not answer the caller, He drew attention to the fact that the clearest proof of His encompassing majesty (*jalāl*) and beauty (*jamāl*), and of His power over the appointed term (*ajal*) for which He created creation, is what He manifested at the beginning of the surah: the origination of the two horizons (*khāfiqayn*, the heavens and the earth) and what is in them of signs apparent to the ear and the eye. So He said, rebuking them for their misguidance in not answering the caller, denouncing them and reproaching them, and guiding by way of an unmentioned antecedent, meaning that the implied sense is: Have these misguided ones not seen (p. 186) the banners of proofs and the clear messages that We set up in this surah, concerning the aims and the means? He linked to it His saying, may He be exalted, as a response to the conclusion of the surah, establishing the return (*ma'ād*) upon its opening, which establishes the beginning with the creation of the two worlds [by the truth: ﴿Have they not seen﴾, meaning: they know with a knowledge that is in its clarity like sight]: ﴿that Allah﴾, and He indicated this greatest Name (*al-ism al-a'ẓam*, the Greatest Name) by His saying: ﴿who created the heavens﴾, with respect to what they contain of lessons that [description] fails to convey, ﴿and the earth﴾, with respect to what it comprises of signs perceived by direct observation and report, ﴿and was not wearied﴾, meaning: was not incapable. It is said: *'iya bil-amr*, when one has not found the way to its intended meaning, or was incapable of it and was unable to perfect it. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said, "'Iyītu bil-amr", when you do not know its way, and "a'yaytu", I became weary. In the *Qāmūs* it says: "A'yā bil-amr" means he became exhausted. ﴿by their creation﴾, meaning: by reason of it; for if any of that had befallen Him, it would have led to deficiency in both of them or in one of them. He emphasized the denial, which implies negation, by adding the preposition in the position of "*anna*" (that), and so He said, may He be exalted: ﴿is able﴾, meaning: with a great, complete and eloquent power, ﴿to give life﴾, meaning: in the manner of renewal, continuously, ﴿to the dead﴾. The matter concerning them, since it is a re-creation, and since they are a small part of what He originated, He mentioned the origination as being of lesser importance and easier in its making.

Since this interrogative denial carries the sense of negation, He answered it with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Yes﴾. They indeed know that He is able to do that, with a knowledge that in its certainty is like sight with the eye, for they know that He is the Originator of that, and that the re-creation is easier than the initial creation according to the customary patterns of their experience. But they are heedless of that, because they turn away from it. And since, along with these clear proofs, which are greater than direct sight, they deny what this making indicates of the encompassing of power, He gave the reason for that, emphasizing it by His saying, establishing power in a general manner that includes the resurrection mentioned at the beginning of the surah, which He stated was the reason He created this creation: ﴿Indeed He, over all things﴾, meaning: He is worthy that power should be related to Him, ﴿is Competent﴾, so that He concludes with what He began with.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 46, verse 34:

When the resurrection (al-ba'th) had been established by the proofs that had been set forth, he reminded them of some of the terrors that occur on its day, as a warning from Him. He said, linking it to what is implied by his statement: Mention to them this (p-188) clear reasoning that conveys the intended meaning, and the admonitions that have passed in this surah. ﴿And the day﴾ — that is: [and] mention the day when ﴿those who disbelieved are exposed﴾ with the easiest of Our commands, ﴿to the Fire﴾ — the presentation of an army before its king — so that they hear its roaring and its groaning, and see its blaze, its flaring and its raging, such that if it were supposed that anyone could die from such a sight, they would die from witnessing it and from the awful vision of it. Those who disbelieved are those who covered over these manifest proofs through their heedlessness and their persistence in it.

When it was as though it were said: What will be done to them at the time of their being presented? It was said, by way of rebuke, reproach and censure: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ — that is: this great matter with which you were threatened, and about which you denied Our messengers in their reports? ﴿The truth﴾ — that is: the established matter to which reality corresponds. So you have no power to escape its burning. It is a matter that you considered an illusion and sorcery, so you did not care for its arrival.

When the attentive listener, who knows what they were displaying of arrogance and insolence, became keenly eager for their answer, He said in His reply, resuming: ﴿They will say﴾ — that is, affirming (p-189) in a situation where affirmation does not benefit: ﴿Yes, indeed﴾ [and] their hastening to deny themselves did not suffice them, until they swore to it, because their state had been distant from acknowledgment; and they mentioned the attribute of Lordship (al-Ihsan), adding to their submission and acquiescence: ﴿and by our Lord﴾ — that is: indeed it is true, it is among the most established of things, and there is nothing in it of what resembles sorcery. Then He resumed the answer to one who asked about their reply [to them] with His words, exalted is He: ﴿He will say﴾ — rebuking them, showing their humiliation in place of their pride that was in the world, which had been caused by their affirmation of this, which they had placed in other than its proper place, and which they had made in the abode of action, whose foundation is belief in the unseen, a denial expressed in a way that conveys the utmost contempt for them: ﴿So taste the punishment﴾ — that is: engage with it as one who tastes with the tongue. Then He stated the cause explicitly, saying: ﴿because you used to﴾ — that is: as a character and a constant nature, always and forever ﴿disbelieve﴾ in the abode of action.

[p. 190] When it became known, from the proofs that have been established and the decisive arguments that have been set up, that this is their end, He made the following statement a consequence of it, as a rejection of what came after the creation of the heavens and the earth at the beginning of the matter concerning the Messenger (ﷺ), and their attribution to him of fabrication, and what follows it: ﴿So be patient﴾, meaning: endure the hardships you see in conveying the message. Al-Qushayri said: Patience (sabr) is to stand firm under the decree of God and to persist without complaint or resentment.

﴿as the possessors of resolve (ulu al-'azm) were patient﴾, meaning: those with determination in the matter (al-jidd fi al-amr) and firmness in earnestness (al-hazm fi al-jidd), with resolute intention and steadfastness from which there is no turning aside. They are those who proceeded in the command of God with such progress as though they had sworn an oath to it, becoming like the lion in its nature and like the strong, brave man surrounded by his tribe. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': Their souls departed from desires and hopes, so they gave their souls to God in truth, because the soul and the heart agreed on the giving.

When the listener became eager to know who they were, He said: ﴿from among the Messengers﴾, upon them be prayers and peace. It has been said, and this is quite clear, that "min" (from among) is for partition (tab'id, i.e. indicating a part), and by them are meant the founders of the revealed laws who strove to establish their foundations and firm up their pillars. The most famous of them are Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, may the prayers and peace of God be upon them all. Some of them compiled them in the verse:

"The possessors of resolve are Noah, the Friend (al-Khalil) son of Azar, Moses, Jesus, and the Beloved Muhammad."

The disagreement over identifying them is widespread and extensive, and this view is the most famous of what has been said about it. All of it is based on "min" being for partition, which is the apparent meaning. The view that they are all the Messengers, [p. 191] was said by Ibn al-Jawzi, and it was said by Ibn Zayd and preferred by Ibn al-Anbari, who said: "min" is for specification of kind (tajnis), not for partition. In one view they are all the prophets except Yunus, upon him be prayers and peace. Ibn al-Jawzi said: al-Tha'labi related it.

When He commanded him with patience, which is among the highest virtues, He forbade him from haste, which is among the mother vices, so that adorning oneself with the virtue of patience, which guarantees success and victory, would be sound. So He said: ﴿And do not seek to hasten (the punishment) for them﴾, meaning: do not seek haste and bring it about by doing something that displeases them at a time other than its fitting time. Since what He commanded and what He forbade is extremely difficult, He made it easy with His statement, as a new sentence (isti'naf): ﴿As if, on the day they see﴾, meaning: in this world at death, for example, or in the Hereafter at the time of the presentation, reckoning, and the greatest, most mighty terror, the reference to which has been strongly made, and the warning of which is given to the people of disobedience, and the good news of which is given to the people of obedience. As for this group, when they see ﴿what they are promised﴾ of the rise of the religion in this world and the resurrection in the Hereafter, and it is made passive because what is hateful is the promise itself, not who makes it, ﴿they will not have remained﴾, meaning: in this world, where they were dominant, ﴿except an hour﴾.

Since "hour" may be meant as a kind (genus) and may also be applied to a long period of time, He established its matter and belittled it with His statement: ﴿of a day﴾. Since what has been mentioned in this surah has undertaken clear proofs and dazzling demonstrations, by explaining what is [p. 192] its intended purpose in such a way that no ambiguity remains, and since its intended purpose leads back to Surat Ibrahim, upon him be prayers and peace, which is monotheism, whose necessary implication is comprehensive knowledge of everything and power over everything, it was concluded with what Ibrahim was concluded with. However, the Ha Mim surahs have a kernel (lubab). The subject and the complement of the predicate have been omitted. It has been said: ﴿A message﴾, meaning: what has been mentioned here is of such clarity and spread of light that it turns back those who are warned and brings them to the pleasure of the Mighty, the Wise, who guarantees everlasting light and lasting bliss. Whoever it does not bring to that, is the one whose wretchedness the Mighty has decreed, so there is no remedy for anyone else in curing him of his great disease. For this reason, He made its being a message a consequence, adding to the conclusion of Ibrahim what suits its opening: ﴿So will be destroyed﴾. It is in the passive form from "ahlaka" (to destroy), because the thing feared is destruction, even if the destroyer is not specified, and to indicate that their destruction is very easy for Him, glorified and exalted be He. ﴿Except the people﴾ who have the capacity to carry out what they attempt of stubborn contention ﴿who are defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾, meaning: those who are deeply persistent in continuously leaving the sphere of what the guide of reason and the original nature calls to, namely obedience, which the transmitted text brings, toward the misleading sin, which both the transmitted text and reason forbid. As for those who committed defiance and those who are defiantly disobedient, the guide of this surah turns them back and brings them to the goal. This latter group is the result of His saying at its beginning: ﴿And those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 3]. [p. 193] The mention of the promised day is the term for which the two horizons (heavens and earth) were created and by which they exist. The indication of power through their creation without fatigue is that He mentioned at the start of them both that they were not created except with truth. The mention of the message is the sending down of the Book from God and His judgment against the defiantly disobedient group with destruction alongside the compassionate guide, and for others with salvation after their flowing into defiance, with repetition, is among the fruits of might and wisdom. So this latter has been fused with that first in the most complete fusion, connected to its meaning like a precious jewel in a firm arrangement, and joined to the first of the surahs that follow it in the best of joinings. Glory be to Him who made it the most noble of speech, as it is the attribute of the King, the All-Knowing, sent down upon the seal of the noble Messengers, and the Messenger of the King, the All-Knowing, may God bless him, his family, his companions, and the people of his noble household, and grant them abundant peace.
